entries.subject: DAMIT 239: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: DAMIT model 239, version 2007-02-27, pole (177°, 17°), period 8.61798 h, taken unchanged from the archive. Mirror solution 240 recorded as an alternative.

entries.subject: Physical scale
entries.finding: 134.65 ± 3.8 km, effective diameter of a sphere fitted to thermal infrared measurements. JPL lists a diameter of 134.65 ± 3.8 km, from the IRAS Minor Planet Survey (PDS data set IRAS-A-FPA-3-RDR-IMPS-V6.0). The thermal sphere diameter is transferred to the mesh as its volume-equivalent diameter.

entries.finding: Shown size Display reference radius "67.33 km (size-calibrated model)" (jpl-small-body-database) differs from the Small Bodies Occultations V4.0 record 349, DAMIT model 239 diameter 149 ± 3 km (volume-equivalent; DAMIT model 239 fitted to 2 occultations); the shown value is kept.

entries.subject: Wratislavia whole-disc color
entries.finding: Gaia Collaboration, Galluccio et al. (2023) published the mean of 16 Gaia epoch spectra of the unresolved disc: reflectance against the Sun in 16 bands from 374 to 1034 nm, 1 at 550 nm (0.966 at 462 nm, 0.989 at 638 nm). The shape is painted in that one color (#454644 in sRGB) through the shared disc-integrated-color method, scaled to the 6% geometric albedo JPL lists (± 0.4%), from the IRAS Minor Planet Survey (PDS data set IRAS-A-FPA-3-RDR-IMPS-V6.0). It is one mean, not a map. Tinaut-Ruano et al. (2023), A&A 669, L14, found Gaia DR3 reflectances slightly too red at wavelengths shorter than 550 nm; the bands are used as published, without that paper's correction.
